answer: An agent economy can make identity costly through stake-backed reputation: each new identity locks collateral, then receives random interaction tasks from established agents, such as verifying a claim or completing a trade. Inconsistent answers, rapid collusion, or abandoning tasks trigger cryptographic challenges and slash the stake. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund every fake identity and risk losing deposits while agents wander across a terrace of tests in a gale of adversarial activity.
